about.title: Built around farmers. Looking toward the future.
about.intro: Abad Limited plans to connect communication, information and supply coordination between farmers, buyers and local entrepreneurs. Our vision is for farmers to develop their own identity and brand alongside their products.
about.vision: Modernize Bangladesh’s agricultural sector through data-driven technology and build a self-sustaining ecosystem where smallholder farmers and everyday buyers across all 64 districts can participate in a strong, transparent and commercially viable network.
missions: Create direct farmer-buyer communication channels that can reduce reliance on intermediaries.
Develop technology-enabled supply chains, contract farming and smart logistics.
Help farmers develop a distinct brand identity through a multi-brand ecosystem.

team.title: Chief Executive Officer
team.bio: Leads Abad’s vision, business direction and growth, with a focus on long-term relationships between farmers, institutional buyers and ecosystem collaborators.
responsibilities: Set the long-term strategy for a data-led platform that helps farmers develop independent brands.
Develop B2B relationships and supply agreements with agro-businesses, corporations, restaurant chains and supermarkets.
Build relationships with potential funding platforms and sponsors for Krishijatra and field initiatives.
Lead Abad’s brand strategy and promotion of its multi-brand ecosystem.

team.title: Chief Technology Officer
team.bio: Responsible for Abad’s digital platform, data systems and technical security, with an emphasis on accessible Bangla experiences and infrastructure that can grow with the network.
responsibilities: Develop the multi-vendor website and app, including farmer profiles, storefronts and order dashboards.
Design livestock tagging software, future IoT integrations and a central farmer database.
Manage scalable cloud infrastructure, secure payment integrations and escrow workflows if approved for implementation.
Create simple Bangla-first interfaces for smallholder farmers and protect platform data.

team.title: Chief Operating Officer
team.bio: Leads field operations, farmer relationships and supply coordination, connecting local hubs, transport arrangements and product quality processes.
responsibilities: Plan and coordinate district and upazila hubs with local agents and dealers toward the 64-district expansion goal.
Coordinate the farm-to-buyer supply chain and owned or shared transport.
Manage field implementation and training for contract farming, solar pumps, drip irrigation and new technologies.
Oversee quality processes across collection, storage and delivery of agricultural produce and livestock.

team.title: Chief Financial Officer
team.bio: Manages financial planning, income and expenditure, capital allocation and company formation, with a focus on practical budgeting and transparent accounting.
responsibilities: Plan and account for potential commission, subscription, trading, logistics and technology-product revenue.
Oversee allocation, accounting, contractual terms and settlement for agricultural funding arranged through approved collaborators.
Control operating costs through local storage and shared logistics, and prepare marketing and transport budgets.
Coordinate company-formation documentation, MoA/AoA, trade licensing, TIN, VAT and tax-related preparation and compliance.

services.title: Connecting production and markets.
services.intro: Each planned Abad service is designed to create a useful connection between farmers, buyers and local entrepreneurs.

items.title: Farmer brands & digital storefronts
items.summary: A planned space for farmer identity, product stories and direct market connections.
items.intro: Abad plans a multi-vendor platform where farmers can establish a storefront with their identity and product information. Buyers will be able to learn about the producer as well as the product.
benefits: An individual storefront and brand identity
An opportunity to receive direct buyer enquiries

items.title: Direct market access & B2B sourcing
items.summary: An initiative to connect producers with restaurants, supermarkets, wholesalers and institutional buyers.
items.intro: Abad will help producers reach buyers beyond local markets and plan supply around demand. Product specifications, quantities, schedules and prices will be agreed through discussion.

items.title: Farm data & livestock traceability
items.summary: Planned farmer, farm and production records with livestock identification tags.
items.intro: Abad aims to maintain relevant farmer and production records in a central database and use unique identification tags for livestock. Information will be shared according to permission, with personal and sensitive records protected.
benefits: Unique livestock identification and permission-based information
Use information to support quality review and planning

items.title: Local hubs & smart logistics
items.summary: A planned network of local hubs and shared transport for coordinated supply.
items.intro: Abad plans collection, storage and distribution hubs with local entrepreneurs and dealers. Coordination between owned vans and other logistics services will focus on managing transport costs and delivery schedules.

items.title: Contract farming & funding connections
items.summary: A planned approach to production coordination, inputs and connections with potential funding collaborators.
items.intro: Abad aims to coordinate production plans with seeds, fertilizer, tools and possible capital support. Eligibility, agreements, funding terms and risks will be assessed separately for each project. Expressing interest through the website does not guarantee funding.

Aim for clear agreements and financial records

items.title: Agricultural inputs & modern technology
items.summary: Access to information on agricultural inputs, tagging tools, solar pumps and drip irrigation.
items.intro: Abad plans to introduce suitable technologies and quality inputs based on farmer needs and develop supply arrangements. Pricing, availability and support will be described for each offer.
benefits: Learn about solar pumps and drip irrigation
Information on tagging tools and equipment

items.title: Training & field demonstrations
items.summary: Learn from technology demonstrations on farms and exchange practical knowledge between farmers.
items.intro: Field demonstrations will show how suitable technologies or improved seeds are used on a farm. The goal is to share practical experience in accessible language and help farmers make decisions suited to their needs.
items.audience: Farmers, agricultural entrepreneurs and training collaborators

items.title: Krishijatra & field initiatives

items.intro: Abad plans to build connections between agricultural ventures, technology providers and potential collaborators through Krishijatra and field initiatives. Details will be published for approved events.

articles.title: When the farmer becomes a brand
articles.excerpt: Connecting a product with its producer’s identity can create opportunities for stronger relationships.
paragraphs: Every agricultural product represents someone’s work, experience and farm. Making that identity visible gives the producer a presence beyond a single supply transaction.
A digital storefront can present production area, product types, seasonality and supply capacity. Accurate, regularly updated information helps buyers start informed conversations.
Abad plans to build an accessible platform for this identity. Its focus will be transparent information, product context and direct communication between producers and buyers.

articles.title: Traceability begins with production records
articles.excerpt: Simple records and reliable identification form a foundation for data-led agriculture.
paragraphs: Recording where a product was grown, when it was collected and what information was added at each stage is an early step toward data-led operations.
A unique livestock tag can connect identity and records. A tag alone does not make the information verified; records also need update and review processes.
Permission-based access is important to Abad’s data plans. Buyer-relevant information and access to a farmer’s personal information will be managed separately.

articles.title: Local hubs, coordinated supply
articles.excerpt: Planning supply around local entrepreneurs and shared transport.
paragraphs: Agricultural supply needs coordination between collection, temporary storage and delivery. A local hub can serve as a point for that coordination.
Involving local entrepreneurs or dealers can help planning reflect local conditions. Storage and handling requirements also vary by product.
Abad is considering a model that combines owned vans with other logistics services. Delivery plans will depend on verified service areas, capacity and timing.

items.a: Abad Limited is an initiative to build a data-led agricultural ecosystem. Its plans include farmer brands, direct market connections, local hubs, smart logistics and technology-enabled agricultural support.

items.q: How can I express interest as a farmer?
items.a: Use the farmer interest form to provide your name, contact details, district and farming activity. After receipt, possible next steps can be discussed. A submitted form does not automatically activate a store or approve an agreement.

items.q: Is Abad already operating in all 64 districts?
items.a: Building a network across 64 districts is our expansion goal. Information about operational hubs and services will be published after it is verified.
A commission or subscription model is under consideration. Applicable fees, included services and settlement terms will be stated in the final offer or agreement.

items.q: How can a business buyer request supply?
items.a: Use the buyer enquiry form to describe your organization, product type, indicative quantity, timing and delivery district. Supply and price arrangements will be discussed separately.

items.q: Can I express interest in becoming a local hub partner?
items.a: Local entrepreneurs and dealers can use the hub-partner form. Potential collaboration will be discussed after reviewing location, facilities and relevant capacity.

items.q: Does submitting an enquiry guarantee funding?
items.a: Funding depends on suitable projects, collaborators, assessment and contractual terms. Website forms are not a loan-approval or investment-payment process.

items.q: What is livestock tagging intended to do?
items.a: Unique tags are intended to connect an animal’s identity with relevant records. Public information will depend on permissions and the service terms.

items.q: Can I purchase products online immediately?
items.a: A multi-vendor marketplace is part of our plan. Product, price, delivery and payment terms will be published before transactions are enabled. Business buyers can express sourcing requirements in the meantime.

items.q: How will my information be used?
items.a: Relevant information will be used to respond to your enquiry or interest and coordinate potential services. Please read the privacy page before submitting a form.

items.q: How can an organization discuss sponsorship?
items.a: Express sponsorship interest on the partners page. A separate proposal can be prepared around approved initiatives, audiences, activities and relevant benefits.

items.q: What does fair pricing mean in this model?
items.a: The aim is to support pricing through direct producer-buyer discussions, quality and demand information, and transparent costs. It does not guarantee the highest price, a fixed income or sale of every product.
